Infrastructure Developer Low-Latency Systems — HFT Technology About the role As an Infrastructure Developer on Zanskar Research's HFT Technology team, you will architect and engineer the ultra-low-latency trading stack that gives our strategies a measurable edge - measured in microseconds and nanoseconds. You will work at the intersection of systems programming, networking, and financial markets, solving some of the most technically demanding engineering problems in the industry. Key responsibilities — Design and develop low-latency order management systems (OMS) and execution infrastructure in C++ (17/20). — Build and optimise kernel-bypass networking components using DPDK, RDMA, or FPGA-based feed handlers for market data ingestion. — Implement and tune exchange connectivity (FIX, ITCH, OUCH, NSE/BSE native protocols) with nanosecond-precision timestamping. — Build and maintain automated testing pipelines including market simulation environments and replay-based regression testing. — Collaborate with quant researchers to deploy new strategies into production with safe, observable rollout processes. — Own reliability and observability: design alerting, circuit breakers, kill-switches, and real-time telemetry dashboards. — Continuously evaluate and integrate new hardware and software technologies to improve throughput and reduce jitter. Required qualifications — Currently pursuing a B.Tech / Dual Degree / M.Tech in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline - with a strong academic record. — Strong C++ proficiency (STL, templates, move semantics, memory model) with a clear understanding of performance implications of language constructs. — Deep knowledge of Linux internals: process/thread scheduling, memory subsystems, system calls, and kernel networking. — Solid understanding of CPU microarchitecture: cache hierarchy, branch prediction, instruction pipelining, SIMD. — Competence in data structures and algorithms - ability to reason about time and space complexity at a hardware level. Good to have — Hands-on exposure to HFT or real-time systems (internship, project, or personal work). — Familiarity with FPGA programming (VHDL/Verilog) or SmartNIC offload pipelines. — Knowledge of exchange market data protocols: ITCH, PITCH, FAST, or NSE/BSE proprietary feeds. — Proficiency in Python for tooling, test automation, and monitoring scripts. What we offer — Access to cutting-edge hardware: co-located servers, 10G/25G NICs, FPGA cards, and dedicated testing environments. — Work on problems where every microsecond genuinely matters - no artificial constraints or bureaucratic bottlenecks. — Rapid ownership: new hires own a production system component within their first 60 days. — Strong engineering culture with regular internal tech talks and hardware deep-dives.(Codeforces/AtCoder 1500+ rating or Codechef 1700+ rating) eligible

Job Description
Infrastructure Developer Low-Latency Systems — HFT Technology About the role As an Infrastructure Developer on Zanskar Research's HFT Technology team, you will architect and engineer the ultra-low-latency trading stack that gives our strategies a measurable edge - measured in microseconds and nanoseconds. You will work at the intersection of systems programming, networking, and financial markets, solving some of the most technically demanding engineering problems in the industry. Key responsibilities — Design and develop low-latency order management systems (OMS) and execution infrastructure in C++ (17/20). — Build and optimise kernel-bypass networking components using DPDK, RDMA, or FPGA-based feed handlers for market data ingestion. — Implement and tune exchange connectivity (FIX, ITCH, OUCH, NSE/BSE native protocols) with nanosecond-precision timestamping. — Build and maintain automated testing pipelines including market simulation environments and replay-based regression testing. — Collaborate with quant researchers to deploy new strategies into production with safe, observable rollout processes. — Own reliability and observability: design alerting, circuit breakers, kill-switches, and real-time telemetry dashboards. — Continuously evaluate and integrate new hardware and software technologies to improve throughput and reduce jitter. Required qualifications — Currently pursuing a B.Tech / Dual Degree / M.Tech in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline - with a strong academic record. — Strong C++ proficiency (STL, templates, move semantics, memory model) with a clear understanding of performance implications of language constructs. — Deep knowledge of Linux internals: process/thread scheduling, memory subsystems, system calls, and kernel networking. — Solid understanding of CPU microarchitecture: cache hierarchy, branch prediction, instruction pipelining, SIMD. — Competence in data structures and algorithms - ability to reason about time and space complexity at a hardware level. Good to have — Hands-on exposure to HFT or real-time systems (internship, project, or personal work). — Familiarity with FPGA programming (VHDL/Verilog) or SmartNIC offload pipelines. — Knowledge of exchange market data protocols: ITCH, PITCH, FAST, or NSE/BSE proprietary feeds. — Proficiency in Python for tooling, test automation, and monitoring scripts. What we offer — Access to cutting-edge hardware: co-located servers, 10G/25G NICs, FPGA cards, and dedicated testing environments. — Work on problems where every microsecond genuinely matters - no artificial constraints or bureaucratic bottlenecks. — Rapid ownership: new hires own a production system component within their first 60 days. — Strong engineering culture with regular internal tech talks and hardware deep-dives.(Codeforces/AtCoder 1500+ rating or Codechef 1700+ rating) eligible

Job Description
Infrastructure Developer Low-Latency Systems — HFT Technology About the role As an Infrastructure Developer on Zanskar Research's HFT Technology team, you will architect and engineer the ultra-low-latency trading stack that gives our strategies a measurable edge - measured in microseconds and nanoseconds. You will work at the intersection of systems programming, networking, and financial markets, solving some of the most technically demanding engineering problems in the industry. Key responsibilities — Design and develop low-latency order management systems (OMS) and execution infrastructure in C++ (17/20). — Build and optimise kernel-bypass networking components using DPDK, RDMA, or FPGA-based feed handlers for market data ingestion. — Implement and tune exchange connectivity (FIX, ITCH, OUCH, NSE/BSE native protocols) with nanosecond-precision timestamping. — Build and maintain automated testing pipelines including market simulation environments and replay-based regression testing. — Collaborate with quant researchers to deploy new strategies into production with safe, observable rollout processes. — Own reliability and observability: design alerting, circuit breakers, kill-switches, and real-time telemetry dashboards. — Continuously evaluate and integrate new hardware and software technologies to improve throughput and reduce jitter. Required qualifications — Currently pursuing a B.Tech / Dual Degree / M.Tech in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline - with a strong academic record. — Strong C++ proficiency (STL, templates, move semantics, memory model) with a clear understanding of performance implications of language constructs. — Deep knowledge of Linux internals: process/thread scheduling, memory subsystems, system calls, and kernel networking. — Solid understanding of CPU microarchitecture: cache hierarchy, branch prediction, instruction pipelining, SIMD. — Competence in data structures and algorithms - ability to reason about time and space complexity at a hardware level. Good to have — Hands-on exposure to HFT or real-time systems (internship, project, or personal work). — Familiarity with FPGA programming (VHDL/Verilog) or SmartNIC offload pipelines. — Knowledge of exchange market data protocols: ITCH, PITCH, FAST, or NSE/BSE proprietary feeds. — Proficiency in Python for tooling, test automation, and monitoring scripts. What we offer — Access to cutting-edge hardware: co-located servers, 10G/25G NICs, FPGA cards, and dedicated testing environments. — Work on problems where every microsecond genuinely matters - no artificial constraints or bureaucratic bottlenecks. — Rapid ownership: new hires own a production system component within their first 60 days. — Strong engineering culture with regular internal tech talks and hardware deep-dives.(Codeforces/AtCoder 1500+ rating or Codechef 1700+ rating) eligible
